golden-circle.name: Golden Circle (Why / How / What)
golden-circle.summary: Simon Sinek's keynote arc: lead with belief, follow with method, finish with proof. Best for brand stories, mission-driven keynotes, and any deck where the audience needs to feel why before they can evaluate what.

beats.name: Why
beats.description: Open with the belief or purpose that animates the work. Why does this exist, and why should anyone care beyond commerce? State it plainly and emotionally — the why is meant to be felt before it is understood.

beats.name: How
beats.description: Translate the belief into the principles that guide how you operate. The values, decisions, and trade-offs that make your approach distinctive. The 'how' is what people who share your why recognize as familiar.

beats.name: What
beats.description: Show the products, services, or outputs that the why and how produce. Concrete examples, not abstractions. The what is the artifact of the belief — proof that the why is more than rhetoric.

beats.name: Proof
beats.description: Demonstrate the impact in lives, customers, or outcomes. Stories beat statistics here; specific people and moments earn the audience's belief better than aggregate numbers. End with proof that what you do works because of why you do it.

beats.name: Invitation
beats.description: Close by inviting the audience to share the belief — to buy, build, join, or evangelize. The strongest invitations don't argue; they assume alignment and offer a way in.

technical.name: Technical
technical.summary: Engineers, data scientists, and technical specialists requiring precision, methodology details, and system-level understanding.
technical.description: Engineers, data scientists, and technical specialists who expect precision, methodology, and system-level understanding. Show the methodology and cite data sources, prefer technical diagrams to metaphors, and do not shy away from dense information. Chart density can be high; 20-40 slides is normal.

candidates.name: Candidates
candidates.summary: Potential hires evaluating company, role, and people.
candidates.description: Candidates are weighing a major life decision and have many alternatives. Lead with mission and why-now, show the team they'll work with, and be honest about the stage. Avoid generic recruiting copy — specifics build trust faster than polish.

plan.name: Plan
plan.summary: Establish a roadmap, operating plan, or sequence of actions with owners and next steps.
plan.description: Use when the deck should turn strategy into coordinated action. Make sequencing, ownership, dependencies, risks, and checkpoints visible.
plan.outcome: The audience understands the plan and accepts the next actions.

casual.name: Casual
casual.summary: Warm, plain-spoken voice for internal updates and customer storytelling.
casual.description: Friendly and direct. Use first- and second-person freely; favor short sentences and contractions. Numbers are still welcome — they just sit alongside human-scale framing rather than leading.
voiceCues: Favor short sentences and active voice.
Frame metrics with a human-scale anchor when possible.
samplePhrases: We shipped the new dashboard last week, and customers are already moving over.
Here's where we ended up on hiring this quarter.
It's been a busy month — here's the recap.

minimal.name: Minimal
minimal.description: A clean, minimalistic theme with a focus on simplicity and readability. Ideal for professional, straightforward presentations.

bold-red.name: Bold Red
bold-red.summary: Confident red and teal accents for urgent, high-salience stories.
bold-red.description: A bold red-led scheme with teal and navy support. Use it when the deck needs urgency, contrast, and clear emphasis.

cool-horizon.name: Cool Horizon
cool-horizon.summary: Cool blue-green palette tuned for professional business decks.
cool-horizon.description: A balanced cool-toned scheme with deep navy, business blues, and teal accents. It works well across strategy, finance, and technical narratives.

poppins.name: Poppins
poppins.description: Poppins is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Poppins for both headings and body text.

aptos.name: Aptos
aptos.description: Aptos is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Aptos Display for headings with Aptos for body text.

cover.name: Cover
cover.summary: The opening slide: title, subtitle and an optional picture.
cover.description: Open a presentation with its subject and a short introduction. Add a picture when it helps establish the context.

text.name: Text
text.summary: Prose. Several blocks sit side by side when short and stack when long.
text.description: Explain one idea in continuous prose. Use paragraphs or flowing blocks for detail that needs to be read in sequence.

chart.name: Chart
chart.summary: One to six charts, with an optional note.
chart.description: Give a chart enough space to show its evidence. Use the title to state the conclusion and labels to explain the measures.

table-beside.name: Table beside
table-beside.summary: A table with commentary beside it.
table-beside.description: Place a table beside its interpretation. Use the supporting text to explain the conclusion without repeating every cell.

timeline.name: Timeline
timeline.summary: Dated events or a roadmap along one axis, with optional notes.
timeline.description: Show events or milestones in chronological order. Label each item with a date or stage and a concise description.

list.name: List
list.summary: Bulleted or numbered points; one long list flows into columns.
list.description: Present several related points in a clear sequence. Use bullets for independent points or numbered items for an ordered list.
